analysis.title: Ad-mageddon Slams Tech, Spikes Spreads; Rates Reprice After Fed Fallout, Macro Maelstrom
key_insights: GOOGL had its worst day ever, worse than the Lehman and COVID sell-offs. Half a trillion dollars of market cap was lost over two days. The stock fell to its lowest since the March 2026 lows and triggered a death cross.
Fortinet, ServiceNow and others also sold off. Broad AI fell 2% and ex-AI rose 1%, ending three days of AI outperformance. NeoClouds fell 5% after three strong recovery days.
NDX fell about 1.5%. Small caps were the only major group to gain. CAT and GOOGL together took 625 points off the Dow. Value strongly outperformed Growth after three days of relative pain.
MSFT surged after hours on a strong beat but ended the day in the red. Goldman traders described the consensus long as a 'source of funds'.

AMZN reported earnings after the close and its results snapped Nasdaq futures down hard. NDX futures were left at key support. Bitcoin rallied off $80k ahead of AMZN EPS and then traded like a high-beta tech stock.
IG credit spreads widened back toward recent wides. Data-center CDS widened and META's Beignet SPV bonds sold off sharply.

UBS traders said the equity tape was healthier than the indices suggest. Capital rotated from crowded AI and Growth into Value, small caps, Consumer and rate-sensitive cyclicals rather than leaving equities, with limited outright shorting and more covering.

Goldman said activity rose to 5 out of 10 with a skew for sale. Long-only funds were net sold $1.5bn. Hedge funds were evenly skewed on very small notionals and bought Comm Services while selling Info Tech, the opposite of long-only funds.

Yields fell 3-6bp, helping housing, Consumer, Financials, Utilities and REITs. Energy stayed offered as crude retreated. Lower yields and weaker crude are accelerating the broadening rather than driving it.

Oil fell on reported outreach from VP Vance to Iranian hardliners and a pledge by a dozen European countries to release 42.6 million barrels by end of January. It recovered after Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf denied progress and Iran reported three tankers hit naval mines in the strait.

WTI found support at $100 and ended only marginally lower, with the Brent contract roll making settlement messy. Shell CEO Sawan said elevated prices 'no longer look like a temporary spike' because fuel inventories have been drawn down quickly.
Diesel fell after Putin affirmed fuel shipments to the US under a quota system. EU natural gas remains at its highest level since 2022.

After the confusing Fed meeting, about 10bps came off terminal 2027 pricing from this week's highs. Sell-side consensus still leans toward more hikes, including as soon as December, because of hot PCE, strong growth and solid jobs data against weak spending and low saving.

Most of the repricing was in 2027, which now prices less than 2 hikes. December hike odds are back at 80% and January hike odds fell to about 35%. The whole curve was bid and the 10Y traded around 5.00% as the curve kept steepening.
The dollar ended unchanged after whipsawing around the ECB decision to hold rates while sounding hawkish. Gold drifted lower toward $4000.

Bloomberg's Simon White noted hedge funds are increasingly hedging long AI stock books with index-level shorts instead of single-name shorts. This supports higher correlation and leaves the VIX more exposed to upside shocks and stocks to deeper declines as firms leverage up for AI capex.

Putin affirmed fuel shipments to the US under a quota system.
